_help.village_economy: Design 5 Oct §EH–§EN (the village economy, by voice). village_cap 24 → 50 (wired: CampSim.cap, §EH pass) (§EI: the band of 25–50 is the harmonious size; 150 is where bosses start, and we stop well short). needs (wired by Claude Code 5 Oct: CampSim._needs, CampNeeds; water trips_per_day is again for every ten folk past the first ten): the six things every camp does every day from the forage rung, by generalists (§EI.1); water is a visible trip like wood (a pot to the spring and back, one piece on the store). trades (wired by Claude Code 5 Oct: Trades, read every sim tick; how each need is read from the land is in sim.trades.gates; the maker's station is the bench of the camp's first non-generalist trade, the kiln and the hearth included, and the kiln stands only with pottery): the seven trades in the order they really arrive (§EI.3); each has a gate (rung, material within reach, an earlier trade) and what it makes visible; generalist true means any adult does it at a bench, false means it makes the maker (§BN). A grown camp shows show_max of them. [NOT WIRED YET] sharing (§EJ): at dusk_form one folk carries a piece OFF the food store to the fire and it is shared out: the store visibly shrinks by what was eaten; the player seated in the circle gets a bowl and a log line once; the hunter never hands out his own kill (§EK); gift_back: after the player has brought the store things, a folk (the record-keeper if there is one) hands the player one made thing, once. hunt (§EK, wired by Claude Code 5 Oct: Hunt, GameCounts, Camps; the region counts are sim.hunt.game, Mike's simple respawn; hunting starts at the storage rung, where the workshop is): a job for an adult with the spear: out past gather reach to where the creature sim says game is, back carrying it whole (over the shoulders, or dragged on a pole by size class); the carcass goes IN the workshop hut and is never seen cut; after process_game_h the animal's pieces appear on their stations from data/animal_use.json, and the food store gains food_units by size class. workshop (§EL, wired by Claude Code 5 Oct: Workshop, Camps, Encampment; the huts blocks' workshop_form, soft, hard, hearth, kiln and porch_sign are read): one hut per camp at the storage rung, two benches under one roof (soft: hide, sinew, cordage, cloth; hard: bone, antler, horn, stone, wood), the hearth outside does meat, fat and lamp oil, the kiln is its own station where there is a potter; benches are stations folk move between, skills distinct (different idles, props, sounds; never both at once); the maker is at a bench most; the player brings materials to the bench that works them; props per people from peoples/*.json huts. Added by Claude Code with the wiring: bench_seats (folk a bench seats), porch_seats, generalist_bench_hours (the one stretch of the gather hours an adult with no maker's role spends at a bench, seeded per folk per day; the rest of the day out gathering, out of sight; the sim's gathering is unchanged), idle_hold_s (how long a bench idle holds), out_m (how far out a gatherer walks before passing out of sight), item_materials (what a carried thing counts as for player_brings_to_bench: reeds and grass are cordage_fibre, branches and logs timber; the hunt's pieces carry their own material, §EK). The kiln stands wherever huts.kiln is non-empty (only_with_trade waits on §EI's trades) and smokes while the maker is a potter at work. [NOT WIRED YET] third_places (§EM): where folk sit when not working: the soak (hot spring within hot_spring_m), the bench under the oldest tree, the flat rock by the water, the hut porch; one idle set; folk there are resting, the gather hours are unchanged. [NOT WIRED YET] library (§EN): a small hut or a lean-to at the storage rung holding the camp book (camp_books.json placement moves here), the found tomes on one wall and the camp's own memory on the other: a winter-count hide (one pictogram a game year from the sim's biggest event) and a knot cord (one knot a folk, colour by stage); neither has text. [NOT WIRED YET] specialists.record_keeper: the fourth face, writes the camp book, sits in the library or walks the camp looking at things. [NOT WIRED YET] fire_circle.idles.night_stories (§EJ.3): telling, night only, gated on a fed fire; the listeners look at the teller. First guesses; the designer owns them.
_help.about: Where camp fires — the safe zones you can wake at after dying — are found (design 29 Sept 2026: only in the rare ruins). Restart after editing.
_help.only_at_ruins: true: camps exist only at inhabited ruins (about half of them) and at the opening encampment; the wild riverside camps and the cliff rock shelters are not placed, and wanderers never make a fire for you. false: the older rule (nearest camp of any kind).
_help.wake_random: true: after a death you wake at a RANDOM inhabited ruin's fire within wake_radius_m of where you died, a different one each time; false: the nearest.
_help.wake_radius_m: How far from where you died the fire can be. If no inhabited ruin lies within it the search widens (x2, up to widen_steps times); failing that you wake at the opening camp.
_help.wake_at_home: Design 30 Sept §AY: true (ambient profile) - after a death you wake at your HEARTH: the opening camp until you make another camp's fire your hearth (right click it). Overrides wake_random. false: the 29 Sept rule.
_help.sim: Design 30 Sept §BL–§BN, the camp simulation. Every number here is a first guess unless the note says 'Mike'; tune by play. tick_game_h: the sim steps once per game hour and catches up missed ticks on load (camps grow while unloaded). store: what a camp banks (wood and food, both VISIBLE as a woodpile and a food store; no HUD) and how many days' worth the folk try to keep. loop: the folk's safe daytime gather loop. population: start 3-5 (Mike), forage_cap, what a fundamental or a crop adds, the tribal ceiling (village_cap 50, §EI; was ~24). births_to_village_cap (Mike, 5 Oct; wired by Claude Code): true lets a camp's own births run all the way to village_cap, food still gating them; forage_cap, fundamental_adds and crop_adds are the ceiling only when it is false. births: need a man and a woman, a surplus, a slow clock; folk have three life stages, child -> teen -> adult (Mike): a child does not gather, a teen gathers at half rate and cannot be a specialist, an adult does both; stage lengths in game days. collapse: what takes a camp — fuel reach stripped, the fire low, the dark walks in; survivors walk to the nearest fire (some got on the way); starvation moves them instead. embers_game_h: a camp fire's embers linger this long so it can be saved. abandon: an empty camp is a ruin after ruin_after_game_days and the forest takes it back over forest_takes_game_days. restraint: take vs regrow. ladder: fire -> food -> storage -> specialist -> exchange; specialists appear at the storage rung (headman, plantkeeper) and where the site allows (maker). wildfire: rare; needs all three.
_help.sim_first_guesses: Added by Claude Code on 30 Sept as first guesses to wire the engine (tune by play): loop.wood_per_gatherer_h and food_per_gatherer_h (units a gatherer brings back per gather hour), loop.walk_out_m (how far the visible loop walks), store.feed_units_per_tick and feed_fire_below_units (folk feed the fire from the woodpile when it drops below this), restraint.woods_units_in_reach (the wood within reach when untouched), regrow_per_game_day (share of it that grows back a day), reach_grow_per_stripped_day_m (the walk lengthens as the woods strip), population.child_eats (share of an adult), fundamental_food_scale and crop_food_scale (what a fundamental or a crop multiplies the food take by), ladder_gates (what moves a camp up a rung), wildfire.fire_prone_biomes, lightning_chance_per_storm_h, spread_m (the burn's reach, by wind and fuel), scar_lasts_game_days, dry_rain_mm_h (less rain than this in a tick keeps the dry spell counting). Retuned 1 Oct after the first sim run: a woodpile unit is one branch's worth of burning whatever the people burn; the folk split their gather hours by what the fire burns and what they eat (not half and half), so a camp of three keeps its fire and a camp of five banks a surplus; the woods in reach regrow slower once stripped. Teens gather at stages.gather_rate; a teen eats as an adult (no number for it yet). population.specialist_gather_rate: a headman, plantkeeper or maker still gathers, at this share of a gatherer (a role, not a job); without it a camp of three with two specialists let its fire die.
_help.opening_jobs_pieces: Design 30 Sept night §BV–§BW (pushed 1 Oct). opening: the opening camp starts with start_folk (4-5, Mike; the elder and the hunter of encampment.gd stay as two of them, the rest are drawn from the people) and the jobs they are seen doing at the spawn. jobs: every folk near the player is in a visible job loop the player can watch complete; the sim's accounting is unchanged, the jobs are that accounting made visible. max_at_once: how many folk work at once at a camp (not one walker per camp); near_player_m: the loops only run within this of the player (unloaded camps tick as numbers). gather.target real_source: a gatherer walks to a real tree with deadfall / a real food plant / the water within loop.gather_reach_m, never a random point, and comes back carrying a visible load (carry_visible) that lands on the store as one piece (trip_adds_piece). feed_fire: takes a piece OFF the woodpile and drops it on the fire when the store is below store.feed_fire_below_units. work_at_hearth: sits by the fire with a prop (the maker's job before there is a maker). child: orbits, follows, never gathers. restore_ruin: at a camp sitting in a ruin, hauls one stone a trip from the heap to the signature (§BQ legibility by hand). store.pieces: EVERY trip adds one visible piece (Mike) — refresh_woodpile adds/removes pieces instead of redrawing from a number; wood_tint source_species: a log takes the bark/wood tint of the species it was gathered from, so the pile is the wood of the place; food_by_life: the food piece each way of life stacks (from each people file's food.preserve), vocabulary in food_pieces. First guesses; the designer owns them.
_help.first_camp: Design 1 Oct §CB (Mike: the first camp's KIND should change too, not only its place). Encampment.candidates scored every land cell on one taste (mild, green, 2 km from a coast, ~20 deg latitude) so the 12 best were all the same kind of place. Now: a new world first ROLLS A KIND (kinds, by weight), then picks a random cell among that kind's candidates_per_kind best cells (at least min_separation_m apart). A kind is a set of biome keys and a water rule (near: river / sea / lake / water, within within_m: a camp needs water, §BL). Every candidate must sit in a biome that offers fuel (fuel.json biomes, needs_fuel), inside temp_c (not lethal), slope under slope_max, elevation inside elevation_m, never in never. Within a kind the score is the old one minus the latitude term: water near, moisture, level ground, a mild mean. The kind also decides the opening camp's people (Peoples.pick by site) and so its fuel, food, store pieces (§BW). A taiga or cold-shore first camp is a harder night one by design. First guesses; the designer owns them.
_help.sim_overrun: (design §CN) Overrun ruins. When the dark empties a camp (its fire out and folk taken: §BL's 'no woodpile and blood', sim.collapse) and it becomes a ruin (sim.abandon), it is overrun if it has a den (needs_den: a delve, §CJ, or a nest's first chamber, §CK). A camp left for hunger is not (from_starving false). On a new world nothing has been taken yet, so a seeded worldgen_share of the old ruins that have a delve start overrun (first guess, Mike to tune); it says nothing about how their people ended (§BQ). The sim never resettles an overrun ruin (sim_resettles false). It is cleared when the fire at its delve's heart is lit (cleared_when; delves.json fire_holders). Lighting the surface hearth gives a safe base but does not clear it (surface_hearth_clears false). Then settlers: after arrive_after_game_h, survivors come back if it fell within survivors_if_fell_within_game_days; otherwise folk (min..max) walk over from the nearest camp within within_km whose population is at least camp_at_share_of_cap of its cap. If that camp later goes dark it is overrun again (relapse). The den itself (who holds it, the night surface, the tells) is delves.json overrun. (design §CO) cleared_when_nest: a nest's den (a cave mouth or grotto the dark took) is cleared by lighting the hearth at its opening, the camp's own gone cold or the old hearth at its remains: the one exception to surface_hearth_clears false, which still holds for delves (Mike, 2 Oct 20:32).
_help.wake_found: (design §DE, wired: Camps.found_fire / camp_at / found_fault, LostDays, Main._found_fire) Waking after a lurker, a fall or the water takes you (3 Oct, Mike by voice: "a random amount ... between one and three days goes by ... whenever you wake up around a hearth, there's other villagers around that find you ... hey, we found you passed out, we're glad you're finally awake"). where: your hearth if you made one (§AY) and it still burns with folk at it; otherwise (no_home) the nearest lit fire with folk at it, measured from where you fell (amends §AY: the opening camp is no longer your hearth by default). A home camp that has gone dark or been overrun is skipped. lost_days: a random span, uniform between the two numbers in game days, so you wake at whatever hour that lands on (§CY.1: after a death you wake at whatever hour it is, into the fire circle or a working camp, §CY.2); the world runs those days the way it runs while you are away (the clock, the moon, the season, the weather, every camp's ticks, plantings, fires burning down, your torch where you fell), nothing faked. Flagged in §DE against §CW (no waiting, no speed-up): the lost days are the one thing that moves the clock past you. log: the line that greets you, with {days} the days that passed rounded to a whole number and written as a word (Two, Three; log_one_day for one); the cause line (hud.json log death_lines) still comes first. death_lines_found: the death lines reworded for a player who is found alive ("Killed by" would read wrong before "we found you"); the waking's cause line uses these, and hud.json log.death_lines where a cause has none here. A hearth whose camp is gone from the world is let go (you have none until you make another); one gone dark, overrun or abandoned is only skipped that waking. The opening camp is the last resort when no lit fire with folk is found within wake_radius_m, widened widen_steps times. What you carried still stays where you fell (§AY).
_help.hearths: A few hearths in every biome, no two alike (Mike, 3 Oct). Hearths are living camps and the old hearths of ruins together. per_land_biome_min: every land biome holds at least this many. km2_per_hearth: big biomes get more, one per this much of the biome's ground (first guess). never_repeat: the sites pass never gives two hearths the same combination of these; with §CS, hearths in different lands always differ in their plants.
_help.fire_circle: Design §CY (seats, pose, idles, the pipe and notice wired by Claude Code, 3 Oct: FireCircle, Camps, Encampment; dawn_break, dusk_form and night wait on §BV's jobs, which aren't built). The fire circle (Mike, 3 Oct: "around the campfire when you spawn they could actually be sitting on the biome appropriate seat like a rock or log. might see them packing a pipe and smoking. just chilling out around the fire"). rest_hours: outside loop.gather_hours every folk who isn't on a job sits in a ring round the fire; this is what a camp does when it isn't working, at every camp, and it is what you wake into at dawn. seats: one seat a person plus spare_seats left empty, in a ring ring_m from the fire, facing it, at least min_gap_m apart; kinds are found things (never built furniture), at most kinds_per_circle of them at one fire; by_biome lists the seats a place can offer, commonest first (an empty list: no camp sits there); wood seats take the bark tint of the stand's dominant species, as the woodpile does (§BW); at_site adds a seat the site itself offers (a fallen block at a ruin camp, the ledge under a cliff shelter) and by_people replaces the list for a people whose fire isn't on the ground (the canopy folk's limb). pose: ONE seated base pose for every cloaked figure (the cloak pools over the seat and hides the legs), with upper-body loops on top; no new rig, no per-species animation (the Falcon/Ganondorf rule): scale and timing do the rest. idles: the loops; who: anyone / adult; weight by phase (dawn, day, dusk, night) is how often a sitter picks it; hold_s how long before picking again; props are small held things; needs is a condition on the camp's real state (an empty food store shows nobody eating; feed_fire is the §BV job and takes a real piece off the pile). pipe: adults only, max_at_once at a fire; the steps in order; it is lit with a brand from the fire, never a spark (§BP: fire is carried, not made); smoke is a few square, posterised puffs on one camera-facing card that rise and drift with the weather's wind at the camp. It is the hearth smoke's family (§CV, smoke.json hearth.look: its colours, flat bands and dither cut-out, pale blue-grey and never a neutral grey), lit by the scene and never glowing; like the column it isn't drawn in the dark beyond the fire's light. The bowl's ember is the one glowing pixel and casts no light. What is in the bowl is not named yet. notice: the hood (only the hood) turns to follow the player inside watch_m, holds, then goes back to the fire; the same values as travellers.json head_look; a dozer doesn't notice. dawn_break: over the last begins_game_h_before_gather game hours before the gather hours begin, the sitters rise one at a time (stretch, stand, take up a basket or bundle, walk out), spread evenly with a little jitter, dozers last; stays_min keep the hearth and the children stay by the fire. dusk_form: from the end of the gather hours, over over_game_h, folk come in carrying, drop the load on the store (the day's last real piece, §BW), sit, and the bowls and the pipe come out. night: keeper_awake stay awake to feed the fire and doze_share of the rest doze where they sit. Nothing here changes a sim tick: it is the camp's rest made visible, as the jobs are its work made visible (§BV). Checked by tools/fire_circle_check.py. First guesses; the designer owns them.

wake_found.log: Folk found you out cold and carried you to their fire. {days} days have passed.
wake_found.log_one_day: Folk found you out cold and carried you to their fire. A day has passed.

food_pieces.fish_on_rack: fish hung on the drying rack, more as the store grows
food_pieces.tubers_in_pit: a lined pit, roots heaped in it
food_pieces.maize_hung: cobs braided by the husk under the roof
food_pieces.grain_in_jars: lidded clay jars by the hut
food_pieces.nuts_in_bark_box: bark boxes hung from the rafters (canopy)

pieces.water_pot_by_hearth: a water pot by the hearth stones, dark with the wet (§EI.1; added by Claude Code with the needs wiring): it lands after the camp's first water trip and stays

child.note: a small figure by the fire; plays, follows the plantkeeper

log.what: a length of fallen trunk laid on its side; two can share it

stump.what: a snapped stump, or a short round of trunk stood on end

root.what: a root standing out of the ground: a cypress knee, a buttress flare, a mangrove prop root

rock.what: a rounded boulder of the place's own stone

flat_stone.what: a slab of the place's own stone: a ledge stone, a slate, a lava plate, a salt crust

driftwood.what: a tide-bleached trunk, pale and barkless; two can share it

hummock.what: a grass tussock, a sedge or moss hummock, or a cut turf

mat.what: a hide or a woven mat on the bare ground, where there is neither wood nor stone to sit on

ruin_block.what: a fallen dressed block off the ruin's heap

limb.what: the great limb the platform is built on (the canopy folk never come down)

column_top.what: the top of a hexagonal basalt column standing a little proud of the causeway's floor (design 3 Oct §DX: a hundred ready-made seats; added by Claude Code)

seats._help_place_first: Design 3 Oct §DX (added by Claude Code): sites whose own seats win over a people's (by_people): the causeway's column tops are the seats whoever lives there.

night_stories.what: telling: hands moving, the hood turning to each listener in turn; the listeners look at the teller instead of the fire

watch_fire.what: sits still and looks into the fire: a slow breath in the shoulders, a shift of weight, the hood tipping

warm_hands.what: both hands out to the fire, turned, rubbed together, held out again

poke_fire.what: leans in and stirs the fire with a stick; the fire's own sparks go up

feed_fire.what: stands, takes a piece off the woodpile, lays it on the fire, sits back down: the §BV job, done from the circle

pipe.what: packs a pipe, lights it with a brand from the fire, and smokes

eat_bowl.what: a bowl lifted to the hood a few times, then set down on the seat

sit_work.what: the hearth-worker's mending and shaping (§BV work_at_hearth, its props), done in the circle

doze.what: the hood sinks and nods, starts, settles again

stretch.what: arms up and out, a roll of the shoulders, on rising

take_up_load.what: shoulders a basket or a carrying bundle from beside the seat

gates._help: Added by Claude Code with the §EI wiring (5 Oct): how each trade's needs are read from the place, within loop.gather_reach_m of the fire (the camp's own map cell and the cells that far out round it). fibre_or_bark_in_reach: a plant of fibre_genera or bark_genera grows in those cells' biomes. clay_in_reach: a clay_soils soil there, or a river or lake within clay_from_water_m (the bank's clay). timber_in_reach: a tree (an emergent or canopy plant) grows there, or the sea's driftwood (the coast within reach). flint_obsidian_or_fine_stone_in_reach: a fine_stone_rocks rock there. fuel_surplus: the woodpile holds fuel_surplus_nights nights' burning (store.wood_units_per_night each). fat_or_oil_or_resin: the hunt's fat (§EK, not built) or a plant of oil_genera, or a resin conifer (techniques.json resin_torch conifer_genera plus resin_genera). fibre_crop_or_wool_herd: the camp herds, or its plot grows a fibre_crop_genera plant. hunt_or_herd: the camp herds (fundamental herd) or it has brought a hunt home (§EK, not built yet). visible_per_trade: how many of a present trade's visible props it adds. Mike, 5 Oct: lighting comes after nothing (§EI.3 asks only fat, oil or resin; it waited on pottery before), and a camp shows cordage first, then its maker's trade with the trades it needs, then the rest in order (Trades.pick_shown). A trade once present stays (sticky) while its rung, its maker and its earlier trades hold: a pottery tradition does not vanish with a thin woodpile.

sharing.player_log_once: They shared their food with you.

hunt.log_once_per_species: The hunters brought back a {creature}. By evening it was a stew, a hide on the frame, and a lamp.

game._help: Added by Claude Code with the §EK wiring (Mike, 5 Oct: 'it just basically respawns if they get too low'; no ecology). GameCounts keeps, per map region (a planet cell), a count of each huntable class whose catalogue species live there (size_class rows of data/creatures; their temp_c and moisture ranges against the region's; water birds and fish where there is water; marine_mammal on a coast colder than marine_max_temp_c, hunted only by marine_peoples). A count starts at capacity; each hunt takes one; a class at its floor is never hunted; a class that falls to its floor is back at capacity respawn_game_days later. trip_m: how far out the hunter goes (between loop.gather_reach_m and reach_m); pause_game_h: the time out there; lamp_nights: how many nights the fat of a hunt keeps the hearth's lamp lit; pieces_decay_game_days: after this the soft and food pieces of a hunt are used up and go, quietly (pieces_stay are kept: bone tools, horn, antler, shell, teeth).

kiln._help: idles added by Claude Code with the §EI wiring: the potter at the kiln, seated at its mouth, shaping a coil pot in the lap or feeding the fire mouth with brush (the maker's station when pottery is the camp maker's trade).

item_materials.material: the item's own material field (the hunt's pieces, §EK)

river_camp._help: Design 4 Oct §ED.1 (added by Claude Code, 5 Oct): the opening is a river camp. on: the rule applies. lat_deg: the temperate band (absolute latitude, degrees) the spawn must lie in, in whichever hemisphere is in spring or summer on day one (the sun is over that side of the equator), so the first day is never shorter than the equinox's. within_m: the fire stands this near a river (its bank, not the water), on any usable land there (the bank's own biome, never one first_camp.never bars); every kind's own water and biome rule gives way to this. flow_m: the river must run on at least this far both upstream and downstream of the camp, so a road can follow it both ways (rivers are short at 1/100 scale: 1 km, measured 5 Oct on seed 7731). folk: how many sit at the hearth (the elder and the hunter, then others). ruin: the camp is a restored hearth inside old broken walls. back_road: a second road leaves the camp the other way along the river, to the nearest ruin that way back_m away.
